authority: Existing authenticated application admits exact human/session/input/consent lineage; module creates no rights receipt or credential boundary
trace: Canonical skeleton.game.trace.v1 complete action/observation/component-reward chain. Human authored collection can begin from a supplied exact environment snapshot; the validator restores/replays actual actions and verifies every observation/reward/terminal/native transition identity.
learning: Actual sparse state/action demonstration counts form a behavioral imitation prior used in control selection, then real offline Q updates use measured environment components. Human preference feedback is a separate authored action-preference prior, not invented environment reward or success.
snapshot: Policy schema skeleton.jeeves.game_learning_policy.v2 adds full bounded imitation counts/strength and source receipt digests in the SAME snapshot, surviving resume/fork separately from Q update/visit counters. Existing runtime code identity fences remain strict; old runtime snapshots require an explicit separately declared migration.
failure: Foreign environment/session/input, malformed or discontinuous trace, rehashed forged observations/rewards, unsupported non-policy controller actions, absent terminal collection reason and exceeded replay/state/count/byte bounds fail explicitly before an episode commit.
limits: Imitation learns authored action preferences; it does not prove task optimality or general game mastery. Consent/source rights are rechecked by application authority at commit, and imported issuer labels grant no trusted provenance.
